findings.observed: banner-en.png ("Financing that fits your plans / Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises.")
findings.expected: Serve a French banner (e.g. banner-fr.png) with "Un financement adapté à vos projets. Taux concurrentiels. Modalités claires. Aucune surprise."
findings.description: The French landing page displays the English banner image with English text embedded in it.
The footer is in English on French pages.
The subtitle uses "tu" while the heading just above it and the rest of the site use "vous".
"Appliquer pour" is a well-known anglicism (calque of "apply for"). Quebec usage is "faire une demande de prêt" or "demander un prêt".
The required-field error under "Nom complet" is in English, while the same error on the other fields is translated.

findings.expected: Let the button grow to fit its label, or shorten it to "Soumettre la demande".
findings.description: The French submit label is clipped. scrollWidth is 290 against a clientWidth of 210, with overflow hidden and nowrap.
The label says "e-mail", which is not standard in Quebec, while the field's own error message says "adresse courriel". The same concept gets two different terms.

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande de 15 000,00 $ a été reçue. (The placeholder name must match the code variable, e.g. {amount}.)
findings.description: The French confirmation shows the raw {montant} token instead of the amount, likely because the placeholder name was translated.
"Balance" for an account balance is an anglicism. The standard banking term is "solde".
In French, zero takes the singular. The English plural rule was applied instead.
The transactions table heading is in English on the French dashboard.
The French transaction dates use the US MM/DD/YYYY format (09/15/2026, 09/12/2026, 09/08/2026), which is ambiguous and wrong for fr-CA. The English version uses ISO.
A bank statement is a "relevé", not a "déclaration", which means a declaration or a filing (e.g. a tax return).
The French dashboard link to the loan calculator points to the English page, so the user switches language.
The French checkbox label means the opposite of the English ("pay now" instead of "pay later"). It also contradicts its own help text about deferring the first payment.
The estimated monthly payment on the French page uses English currency formatting (leading $ and a decimal point).

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Charges" was translated in its legal sense ("accusation", a criminal charge) instead of meaning fees ("frais").

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve de l'approbation du crédit.
findings.description: The French rate note drops the "subject to credit approval" condition.

findings.expected: Use the French version of promo-a showing "Taux variable : 5,2 %"
findings.description: The French promo image shows a different offer (a fixed rate of 4.9%) from the English one and from its own alt text and the page text (variable rate of 5.2%).
"Close" was translated as the adjective "proche" (near) instead of the verb "fermer".
The French application confirmation page declares its document language as English, unlike the other French pages, which declare fr-CA.

findings.observed: Not Found — The requested URL was not found on the server. If you entered the URL manually please check your spelling and try again.
findings.expected: Provide a localized 404 page, e.g. "Page introuvable — La page demandée n'existe pas."
findings.description: Unknown URLs under /fr/ show the framework's default English 404 page, with no localization.
